explanation.en: Use the arrow keys to slide a square ball around a paddle. It should change colour only while their rectangles overlap. This is the collision model we will use for Pong: a rectangular hitbox around the ball, rather than a mathematically exact circle.
explanation.nl: Gebruik de pijltjestoetsen om een vierkante bal rond een paddle te schuiven. Die mag alleen van kleur veranderen wanneer de rechthoeken overlappen. Dit is het botsingsmodel voor Pong: een rechthoekig raakvlak rond de bal, geen wiskundig exacte cirkel.

body.en: overlaps(ball, paddle) receives two sequences in (left, top, width, height) order and returns a Boolean. pygame.Rect can be constructed from such a sequence. Rect.colliderect(other) checks for a nonempty overlapping area. Merely touching edges is not overlap. Both horizontal and vertical ranges matter; a ball passing above a paddle should miss.
body.nl: overlaps(ball, paddle) ontvangt twee reeksen in de volgorde (links, boven, breedte, hoogte) en geeft een Boolean terug. pygame.Rect kan uit zo’n reeks worden gemaakt. Rect.colliderect(other) controleert op een overlappend gebied met oppervlakte. Alleen rakende randen zijn geen overlap. Zowel horizontale als verticale bereiken tellen mee; een bal boven een paddle moet missen.

import asyncio
import pygame
import rules

async def main():
    pygame.init()
    screen = pygame.display.set_mode((640, 400))
    clock = pygame.time.Clock()
    font = pygame.font.Font(None, 28)
    running = True
    paddle = pygame.Rect(280, 140, 12, 120)
    x, y = 320.0, 190.0
    while running:
        for event in pygame.event.get():
            if event.type == pygame.QUIT or (event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN and event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE):
                running = False
        dt = min(clock.tick() / 1000, 0.05)
        keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
        x += (int(keys[pygame.K_RIGHT]) - int(keys[pygame.K_LEFT])) * 140 * dt
        y += (int(keys[pygame.K_DOWN]) - int(keys[pygame.K_UP])) * 140 * dt
        ball = pygame.Rect(round(x), round(y), 16, 16)
        touching = rules.overlaps(list(ball), list(paddle))
        screen.fill((16, 23, 39))
        pygame.draw.rect(screen, (80, 180, 255), paddle)
        pygame.draw.rect(screen, (255, 145, 50) if touching else (255,255,255), ball)
        pygame.display.flip()
        await asyncio.sleep(1 / 60)
    pygame.quit()

asyncio.run(main())
files.rules.py:
import pygame

def overlaps(ball, paddle):
    ball_rect = pygame.Rect(ball)
    paddle_rect = pygame.Rect(paddle)
    return ball_rect.left < paddle_rect.right

    font = pygame.font.Font(None, 28)
    running = True
    paddle = pygame.Rect(280, 140, 12, 120)
    x, y = 320.0, 190.0
    while running:
        for event in pygame.event.get():
            if event.type == pygame.QUIT or (event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN and event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE):
                running = False
        dt = min(clock.tick() / 1000, 0.05)
        keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
        x += (int(keys[pygame.K_RIGHT]) - int(keys[pygame.K_LEFT])) * 140 * dt
        y += (int(keys[pygame.K_DOWN]) - int(keys[pygame.K_UP])) * 140 * dt
        ball = pygame.Rect(round(x), round(y), 16, 16)
        touching = rules.overlaps(list(ball), list(paddle))
        screen.fill((16, 23, 39))
        pygame.draw.rect(screen, (80, 180, 255), paddle)
        pygame.draw.rect(screen, (255, 145, 50) if touching else (255,255,255), ball)
